name: MathlibAnnex.PluckerRecovery.nonempty_linearCertificate_of_pluckerBodies_eq
title: Almost-contractive linear recovery with exact volume scaling

content.display_title: Almost-contractive linear recovery with exact volume scaling
content.one_sentence_role: Recovers one bijective linear factor with a norm estimate and exact volume scaling.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $n=m+1>0$ and $V=\mathbb R^n$ with the reference sup norm and standard Lebesgue measure $\lambda$. The continuous norms $p,q$ have fixed positive comparison constants
$$a_p\|x\|_\infty\le p(x)\le b_p\|x\|_\infty,\qquad
a_q\|x\|_\infty\le q(x)\le b_q\|x\|_\infty.$$
Set $K_p=\{x:p(x)\le1\}$, $K_q=\{x:q(x)\le1\}$ and $v_p=\lambda(K_p)$, $v_q=\lambda(K_q)$, as positive finite real numbers. For a real linear map $A:V\to\mathbb R^N$, let $A_{ij}=(Ae_j)_i$ be its matrix in the standard bases. The minor-coordinate space has one coordinate for each increasing $n$-tuple $I$ of distinct rows from $\{1,\ldots,N\}$, and
$$\Pi_n(A)_I=\det(A_{I,*}).$$
Define the signed generator set and its real convex hull by
$$\begin{aligned}
\mathcal G_p^N
 &=\left\{\sigma v_p\Pi_n(A):\begin{array}{l}
       A:V\to\mathbb R^N\text{ is real linear},\ \sigma\in\{1,-1\},\\
       \|Ax\|_\infty\le p(x)\quad(x\in V)
       \end{array}\right\},\\
\mathcal P_p^N&=\operatorname{conv}_{\mathbb R}\mathcal G_p^N.
\end{aligned}$$
Define $\mathcal G_q^N,\mathcal P_q^N$ in the same way using $q,v_q$. The generators are vectors of minors, not linear maps. Suppose $\varepsilon>0$ and $\mathcal P_p^N=\mathcal P_q^N$ for every $N$. There exist $r\in\mathbb N$, real linear maps $B_p,B_q:V\to\mathbb R^{n+r}$, a real linear bijection $L:V\to V$ with
$$B_qL=B_p,\qquad \operatorname{range}B_p=\operatorname{range}B_q,$$
$$\forall x,\ (1-\varepsilon)q(Lx)\le p(x),\qquad
v_p|\det L|=v_q.$$
content.assumptions: The coordinate dimension is positive. The inputs are the norms $p,q$ with the stated positive comparison bounds, $\varepsilon>0$, and equality $\mathcal P_p^N=\mathcal P_q^N$ for every nonnegative $N$. The nonzero leading minors used in the proof are obtained during the construction, not assumed.
content.conclusion: The same bijection $L$ factors the selected representatives and satisfies both the norm estimate and the exact volume equation. No upper restriction $\varepsilon<1$ is required.
content.proof_summary: Anchor the common raw point at a nonzero leading coordinate, recover its chart factor, and compute the estimate and volume identity for that factor.

proof_steps.text:
**Anchor the same representatives.** Let $D_q>0$ be the maximum absolute determinant of a family of $n$ real linear functionals dominated by $q$, and choose target satellite parameters with $\eta=D_q/2$. The absolute maximizing target base has
$$|\det M_{F_q}|\ge D_q-\eta>0.$$
Thus every target support maximizer has nonzero leading minor coordinate, by [the leading-coordinate lemma](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/RecoveryCertificate.lean#L227-L272). [anchored common raw selection](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/RecoveryCertificate.lean#L300-L336) supplies one $z$ and the same contractive $B_p,B_q$, with signs $\sigma_p,\sigma_q\in\{1,-1\}$, the target condition $1-\varepsilon<\|B_qx\|_\infty$ whenever $q(x)=1$, and
$$z=\sigma_pv_p\Pi_n(B_p)=\sigma_qv_q\Pi_n(B_q),\qquad z_{I_0}\ne0.$$
Here $I_0=(1,\ldots,n)$ selects the first $n$ rows. Let $S_p=(B_p)_{I_0,*}$ and $S_q=(B_q)_{I_0,*}$ be the corresponding square matrices. Both are nonsingular because their determinants give the nonzero coordinate $z_{I_0}$, up to nonzero signs and volumes. Put $\tau=\sigma_p\sigma_q$. Each coordinate gives
$$v_p\det(B_p)_{I,*}=\tau v_q\det(B_q)_{I,*}.$$
This is [the weighted minor relation](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/RecoveryCertificate.lean#L450-L484). Its nonzero anchor uses the determinant gap, including when $\varepsilon\ge1$.

**Recover the factor, row by row.** Put
$$c=\tau v_q/v_p\ne0,\qquad L=S_q^{-1}S_p.$$
The maximal minors of $B_p$ are $c$ times those of $B_q$. The same proportionality holds for any ordered row selection: sorting contributes the same permutation sign on both sides, and a repeated row makes both determinants zero. This is [the passage from increasing to ordered minors](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/MaximalMinorFactorization.lean#L309-L324).

Fix corresponding row vectors $u_p$ of $B_p$ and $u_q$ of $B_q$. Applying the proportionality to the leading block and to its $i$th-row replacement gives
$$\det S_p=c\det S_q,\qquad
  \det S_p[i\leftarrow u_p]=c\det S_q[i\leftarrow u_q].$$
Row Cramer gives each coordinate of the two normalized rows. Substituting both proportionalities, with $c,\det S_p,\det S_q\ne0$, gives
$$\begin{aligned}
(u_pS_p^{-1})_i
 &=\frac{\det S_p[i\leftarrow u_p]}{\det S_p}\\
 &=\frac{c\det S_q[i\leftarrow u_q]}{c\det S_q}\\
 &=\frac{\det S_q[i\leftarrow u_q]}{\det S_q}\\
 &=(u_qS_q^{-1})_i.
\end{aligned}$$
This is the source's [row-coordinate calculation](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/MaximalMinorFactorization.lean#L136-L177) for these two matrices and this fixed row. Equality in every coordinate now yields
$$\begin{aligned}
u_p
 &=(u_pS_p^{-1})S_p\\
 &=(u_qS_q^{-1})S_p\\
 &=u_q(S_q^{-1}S_p)=u_qL.
\end{aligned}$$
Thus $B_qL=B_p$ on all rows, as recorded by [the chart factor theorem](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/MaximalMinorFactorization.lean#L335-L344). Both leading blocks are nonsingular, so this same $L$ is invertible by [chart factor invertibility](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/MaximalMinorFactorization.lean#L346-L355). Since $L$ is onto,
$$B_p(V)=B_q(L(V))=B_q(V).$$
For fixed $B_p,B_q$ the factor is unique: $B_qL'=B_p$ implies $S_qL'=S_p$, hence $L'=S_q^{-1}S_p=L$. This uniqueness concerns the fixed representatives, not all possible choices of them.

**Evaluate the same factor in the norm estimate.** If $x\ne0$, injectivity gives $Lx\ne0$. Homogeneity of the target lower condition at $Lx$ gives
$$(1-\varepsilon)q(Lx)<\|B_qLx\|_\infty
=\|B_px\|_\infty\le p(x).$$
If $x=0$, both sides are zero. The resulting universal non-strict estimate is [the factor model bound](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/RecoveryCertificate.lean#L815-L821). There is no division by $1-\varepsilon$.

**Compute its determinant and volume.** The leading minor of $B_qL=B_p$ gives $\det S_p=\det S_q\det L$. Substitute into the weighted leading-minor relation:
$$v_p\det S_q\det L=\tau v_q\det S_q.$$
Cancel $\det S_q\ne0$ to obtain $v_p\det L=\tau v_q$. Taking absolute values, using $v_p,v_q>0$ and $|\tau|=1$, gives
$$v_p|\det L|=v_q.$$
The [signed determinant identity](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/RecoveryCertificate.lean#L913-L929) and [absolute volume identity](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/RecoveryCertificate.lean#L932-L939) use this same factor.

content.lean_realization_notes: Factor uniqueness in the proof is for fixed anchored representatives; the public certificate only asserts existence. It does not publicly store the intermediate maps’ two contractivity fields. Different common-point selections can differ.
